rows.title: Housing market affordability is so bad that Zillow says it will take you 13.5 years to break even on a purchase from July onward
rows.standfirst: This “crucial milestone” that signifies financial stability will be lost on new homeowners for more than a decade.

rows.title: You can either have a high-paying job or an affordable house. Getting both is the housing market Catch-22
rows.standfirst: “You’ll get higher wages, but then you have to pay enough in extra housing costs,” says Berkeley’s Jesse Rothstein. “You lose all of those extra earnings that you get.”

rows.title: Blockbuster economic data from last few weeks has made Fed’s rate announcement today that much harder: ‘The Fed has to talk tough’
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve is set to leave interest rates unchanged for the second time, but a final rate hike isn’t off the table.

rows.title: Jerome Powell’s Federal Reserve is still on pause when it comes to rate hikes—for now
rows.standfirst: The central bank left the door open to further rate hikes if inflation pressures should accelerate in the months ahead.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon just used one of Warren Buffett’s most famous quotes to warn about higher-for-longer interest rates
rows.standfirst: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon isn’t holding out for a drop in the base rate—instead he’s making sure his bank won’t be left “swimming naked.”

rows.title: Home prices in 7 cities just reached all-time highs on the back of a blistering 7-month run for the housing market—and the Midwest is the big winner
rows.standfirst: It’s good to own in Detroit and Chicago right now, but not so much in San Francisco and Seattle.

rows.title: Americans are taxed $60 billion in real-estate commissions, says attorney who just won a $1.8 billion mega-verdict against National Association of Realtors
rows.standfirst: Stephen Brobeck, senior fellow at the Consumer Federation of America, says buyer agent’s commission are effectively added in, “inflating the sale price.”

rows.title: U.S. economy adds 150,000 jobs in October, likely down about 30,000 on auto strikes alone
rows.standfirst: The economy looks solid, especially considering September’s 9.6 million job openings, down from 2022’s record 12 million but high by historical standards.

rows.title: Santa Fe’s ‘mansion tax’ wouldn’t even touch the first $1 million on a sale price, but many realtors and residents still say it’s too extreme
rows.standfirst: On a $1.2 million home sale, the new tax would apply to $200,000 in value, with $6,000 going to the city’s affordable housing trust fund.

rows.title: Google’s ‘San Francisco Project’ wanted to build 15,000 homes in the Bay just 3 years ago, but the deal is off—for now
rows.standfirst: Tech giant and LendLease terminate agreement for $15 billion project, but Google is keeping the plans alive.

rows.title: Remote workers in Australia just got a stark warning from an Indian investor: Your job is ripe for outsourcing
rows.standfirst: Remote-work jobs could be filled more efficiently by Indian workers at 10% to 15% of an Australian employee’s salary, says Indian investor.

rows.title: Mortgage rates are dropping fast after a shock jobs report set off a series of dominoes on Wall Street—The housing market can thank Detroit’s striking auto workers
rows.standfirst: To all the homebuyers dreading the toxic mix of low inventory and 8% mortgage rates, how does a cooling economy and a 7.4% rate sound?

rows.title: 40-year-old dad who has bought and sold 3 homes doesn’t see how he can save enough for this housing market: ‘It’s not avocado toast’
rows.standfirst: Jacob Fuerst and his wife make $200,000, but childcare, energy and rental fees are too high. “It just feels unfair that I held up my end of the bargain.”

rows.title: Carmakers are struggling to make electric vehicles affordable for pinched consumers—and rethinking their investments amid sagging demand
rows.standfirst: Ford and GM’s move to adjust EV production plans “raise deeper concerns” around their ability shift away from gasoline-powered vehicles.

rows.title: Venice Beach artist’s small photo series balloons into series tackling urban crisis: ‘Where Has All The (affordable) Housing Gone?’
rows.standfirst: Judy Branfman’s exhibit laments how the once bohemian neighborhood has changed over the decades and tracks disappearing rent-controlled units.

rows.title: Americans pay $100 billion in real estate commissions but get ready for a 30% cut on that, expert says
rows.standfirst: A $1.8 billion verdict this week against the National Association of Realtors and large brokerages likely spells changes ahead.

rows.title: Housing affordability is so strained that 1 in 5 couples ask for down payment cash on their wedding registry. Your friends and family would rather give you cash to go to Mexico
rows.standfirst: Home prices are soaring, and down payment funds are becoming popular wedding registry items. But couples receive more on average asking for a honeymoon.

rows.title: Millennials led the consumer fintech revolution post-2008. Here’s why Gen Zers are about to do the same
rows.standfirst: The ground is shifting again–and it looks strikingly similar to the early 2010s.

rows.title: The housing market is starting to crack—Sellers are cutting prices at record levels as ‘You can no longer price based off of where sales were’
rows.standfirst: Nearly 7% of sellers posted price drops in October, Redfin says—well above the 3.6% average.

rows.title: The rich are fleeing the climate crisis by scrambling to buy chalets in the Alps
rows.standfirst: They might find there’s no escape. Rising temperatures in European mountain ranges are increasingly making for an unpredictable ski season, and might hurt wealthy buyers’ investments.

rows.title: From Wall Street to Main Street and tax cuts to bailouts, BofA just dropped a list of 15 huge changes for investing in the 2020s
rows.standfirst: Goodbye capital, hello labor. Au revoir tax cuts, bonjour bailouts. And finally, farewell to deflation, and a weary welcome to inflation.

rows.title: Consumers have been propping up the U.S. economy when no one else could—now the debts are being called and they can’t pay their bills
rows.standfirst: Americans’ credit card balances have hit a record high.

rows.title: SoCal housing is so unaffordable that billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott has made yet another multi-million dollar donation to fix the problem
rows.standfirst: Scott donated $15 million to Culver City, Calif.-based Century Housing.

rows.title: Millennials and Gen Z say it’s harder to buy a house and get promoted than it was for their parents
rows.standfirst: 55% of young people say it’s harder to buy a home than it was for their parents—and harder to get ahead in the office.

rows.title: The ‘silver tsunami’ is about to hit the housing market—but millennials and Gen Zers may not come out any better in the wash
rows.standfirst: Just over half of people aged 50-plus are set to downsize in the next two years.

rows.title: Airbnb guests are unwittingly renting houses in Florida from an unusual host: One of the world’s largest private-equity firms
rows.standfirst: Homes listed for Airbnb nightly rentals are, surprisingly, owned by TPG, the world’s sixth largest private-equity firm.

rows.title: The cracks in the housing market are growing larger as sellers slash prices, Redfin says. But beware the all-cash bids
rows.standfirst: Mortgage rates are down slightly, the number of homes for sale is up, and sellers are dropping their asking price, according to a new Redfin report.

rows.title: Inflation means your grocery bill has skyrocketed ahead of Thanksgiving. Here’s how prices have changed—and why it’s so expensive
rows.standfirst: The price of turkey may have dropped, but Americans will still see higher grocery costs ahead of Thanksgiving.

rows.title: Despite the wave of boomers returning to work after the Great Retirement, there are still 2 million more retirees than America’s workforce can handle
rows.standfirst: Retirees aren’t coming off the sidelines to rescue America’s employers.

rows.title: Morgan Stanley’s investment chief expects stocks to rise just 2% in all of 2024—but these AI-era picks and defensive plays could help investors outperform
rows.standfirst: “The leading macro data suggests that we’re in a late cycle market environment,” Morgan Stanley’s Wilson wrote Monday, adding that it’s stock pickers’ world.

rows.title: This chart shows why millennials, the biggest generation in American history, will keep housing prices sky-high for years to come
rows.standfirst: “The crux of the issue is supply,” says Ned Davis Research. Too many millennials chasing too few homes leads to housing market inflation.

rows.title: Millennials are replaying their parents’ housing market journey as first-time buyers in their 30s flood into an unaffordable market
rows.standfirst: First-time buyers make up 32% of all homebuyers, the National Association of Realtors says—up from last year’s historic low of 26%.

rows.title: The revenge of the blue-collar worker: Bidenomics is working too well and Democrats’ bourgeois base is souring on it
rows.standfirst: The upper-middle class is restless.

rows.title: This couple was so miserable with a 2.5-hour super-commute, they took on an extra $1,200 monthly mortgage payment: ‘We’d do it again in a heartbeat’
rows.standfirst: “This is definitely a short-term play for us, this isn’t a forever home,” Dennis Stalmack says. “We bought with what was out there. But we’re not upset with it.”

rows.title: Forget the gloom of the 1970s—UBS thinks the U.S. economy is headed back to a Clinton-like era of the bustling 1990s
rows.standfirst: “The bottom line: Something is afoot with the US economy,” wrote UBS’s Jason Draho.

rows.title: Consumer inflation stayed flat in October thanks to cheaper gas, which slowed overall price increases
rows.standfirst: Lower gas prices helped cool overall inflation, which was unchanged from September to October, down from a surprise 0.4% jump the previous month.

rows.title: Wall Street surges on cool inflation report, with S&P 500 rising to highest level in 2 months
rows.standfirst: “Ain’t no reason to believe the last inflation mile will be the most difficult,” said EY Chief Economist Gregory Daco.

rows.title: Stocks soar as Wall Street celebrates a cooler-than-expected inflation report that may signal an end to Fed rate hikes: ‘The immaculate disinflation continues’
rows.standfirst: “The Fed is increasingly likely to be in a position to cut rates in the second quarter of 2024,” Lazard’s chief market strategist says.

rows.title: This isn’t your parents’ first-time homebuyer: more millennials are breaking into the housing market, but they’re older than boomers were and need to earn a lot more money
rows.standfirst: Despite millennial plight, 32% of buyers this year bought their first house.

rows.title: Wholesale prices had their biggest drop in over 2 years, another sign inflation is fading away
rows.standfirst: The producer price index showed its first decline since May and its biggest drop since 2020—a sign that prices are cooling before they reach consumers.

rows.title: Wholesale inflation just had its largest monthly drop in 2.5 years: ‘We got more Goldilocks today’
rows.standfirst: Producer prices dropped in October in what investors hope is a sign of a long-awaited economic turnaround.

rows.title: Lower inflation may be the hammer that cracks the unaffordable housing market for would-be homebuyers
rows.standfirst: Inflation slowing to 3.2% last month means home shoppers may benefit from stabilizing consumer prices and cheaper mortgages, if the Fed cuts interest rates.

rows.title: Burberry joins LVMH and Gucci in the luxury slump as brand says it may miss its revenue target for the year
rows.standfirst: Burberry’s half-year sales inched up just a little, pointing to a luxury downturn that its rivals like LVMH and Kering have been experiencing.

rows.title: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin bashes Bidenomics as debt-reliant, inflationary policies: ‘The American public knows things aren’t working in this economy for them’
rows.standfirst: “Whoever told him to run on Bidenomics has no idea how to read an economics textbook,” the Wall Street titan said.

rows.title: Cathie Wood says forget inflation, deflation is the real enemy after the Fed hiked rates too far, too fast: ‘Investors are worrying about the wrong thing’
rows.standfirst: “I think the Fed’s overdone it. I think we’re going to see a lot more deflation going forward,” the ARK Invest CEO and founder said this week.

rows.title: Target gains $9 billion in market cap despite falling sales last quarter, as Wall Street gets an up-close look at the health of the American consumer
rows.standfirst: But Target’s 20% stock bump from its earnings still leaves it 14% down from the beginning of the year, or $17 billion.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs dismisses Deutsche Bank and UBS comparisons of the 2020s to other eras: The tactic is ‘too simple’ and likely to be wrong
rows.standfirst: Goldman Sachs’s Jan Hatzius and David Kostin outlined during a roundtable why their firm is so optimistic about 2024.

rows.title: Mortgage rates have been falling for weeks as inflation fades—but the housing market may still struggle with affordability and high home prices
rows.standfirst: “For those homebuyers who can wait, the spring will bring more new listings and lower mortgage rates,” Bright MLS chief economist Lisa Sturtevant said.

rows.title: Housing math just isn’t mathing, a Fed president says, ripping into NIMBYism and homes that are ‘increasingly unattainable for too many workers’
rows.standfirst: Tom Barkin, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, sees math that doesn’t add up for too many—and he thinks “NIMBYism is real.”

rows.title: Why are housing prices up 242% in Boise and only 73% in Baltimore since 2012? These 4 factors are driving prices says a noted expert who studied 100 markets
rows.standfirst: Analysis from the American Enterprise Institute helps explain housing’s remarkable resilience. Three of the fundamental factors are still working in favor of a robust market.

rows.title: Americans are upset about surviving a pandemic and paying for the privilege: ‘They want these prices to be back where they were’
rows.standfirst: “Most Americans,” says Lisa Cook of the Federal Reserve Cook said, “are not just looking for disinflation. They’re looking for deflation.”

rows.title: The housing market may be at a standstill–Americans are growing more psychologically attached to their homes than ever
rows.standfirst: In the face of ongoing economic and geopolitical uncertainty, the notions of ‘home’ and a trusted and safe community have become more resonant than ever.

rows.title: The housing market is crazy expensive, but ‘an improvement in affordability that we have only seen a handful of times over the past ~35 years’ is coming, says Morgan Stanley
rows.standfirst: “The evolution of the U.S. housing market has been Herculean or devastating depending on where you look,” the strategists wrote in their forecast.

rows.title: After Amsterdam told young British men to ‘Stay Away,’ the Dutch housing crisis prompts a new message: Less sex, drugs and profits
rows.standfirst: The center-right leads as voters go to the polls for Wednesday’s elections: “Not everything can be done everywhere at the same time.”

rows.title: With inflation cooling and AI hitting its stride, stocks are on the cusp of record-setting ‘Roaring 2020s,’ Ed Yardeni says
rows.standfirst: A 4,600 price target for the S&P 500 might have been “too conservative,” the veteran market watcher says.

rows.title: Housing market analyst ‘Poison Ivy’ Zelman, who called the 2008 bust that led to the Great Financial Crisis, sees ‘extremely depressed levels’ of existing home sales for years
rows.standfirst: Existing home sales dropped 14.6% in October on a year-over-year basis—a new 13-year low.

rows.title: RE/MAX chairman on his 8th housing recession and settling out of the $1.8 billion antitrust verdict: ‘I’ve never seen this before in my career’
rows.standfirst: Dave Liniger on what will happen to real estate commissions after the bombshell antitrust verdict: “I wish I could tell you; I have no idea.”

rows.title: Beer, wine, cocktails: Here’s how climate change is imperiling our Thanksgiving booze
rows.standfirst: Our favorite drinks are in trouble. Big trouble.

rows.title: Wealthy six-figure earners who kept the economy chugging along are starting to pinch pennies, signaling the post-COVID spending boom may be over
rows.standfirst: “Thrifty behavior has been climbing up the income ladder,” reads a note from Morgan Stanley.

rows.title: ‘To buy or not to buy, that is the question’: BofA reveals rent is cheaper than mortgages in all but two of 97 major metros
rows.standfirst: Homebuyers have been suffering the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune of late.

rows.title: ‘That’s not a Black Friday deal’: Pinched shoppers hold out for deeper discounts—boding ill for earnings
rows.standfirst: Consumers aren’t spending at the same pace they did during the past couple of years, when the holidays were marked by post-pandemic splurges.

rows.title: Biden’s new supply chain council is trying to bring down inflation—a key challenge in his 2024 presidential run
rows.standfirst: Supply chain problems fueled higher inflation as the U.S. recovered from the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021.

rows.title: Late 2023 recession off a ‘classic policy-led boom-bust cycle’ is already happening, Deutsche Bank says—but AI is changing the game a bit
rows.standfirst: “We think our narrative still holds,” Deutsche Bank economists warned Monday, arguing the mild recession is already “materializing.”

rows.title: ‘Dr. Doom’ Nouriel Roubini warns the market is in for a ‘mega-threatened age’ and investors will lose trillions: ‘This bloodbath is likely to continue’
rows.standfirst: “Our first priority will be to survive the next few decades of instability and chaos.”

rows.title: Home prices are likely to drop next year, but don’t expect that to solve the affordability crisis, bank exec says
rows.standfirst: Morgan Stanley forecasts a 3% drop in home prices next year—just half of the 6% price increase this year.

rows.title: Biden touts ‘progress’ on inflation as he takes aim at ‘junk fees’ and corporate ‘price-gouging’ in first meeting of supply chain council
rows.standfirst: “We know that prices are still too high for too many things, that times are still too tough for too many families,” Biden said. “But we’ve made progress.”

rows.title: Job-market optimism pushed consumer confidence up for the first time in four months in November
rows.standfirst: The share of consumers who said jobs were “plentiful” rose, and more people said they expect to buy a car, a home or major appliances.

rows.title: The high mortgage rates locking you out of the housing market aren’t going away, top economist says. ‘Everybody should get used to 5.5% to 6%’
rows.standfirst: “Everybody should get used to 5.5% to 6%, because that’s where mortgage rates are going to settle in, [in the] long run,” Zandi said.

rows.title: Ikea stores owner plans to spend $1.1 billion to cut prices next year in the latest sign of global deflation: ‘Ikea is made for crisis’
rows.standfirst: Ingka Group’s Deputy CEO said people were buying more storage solutions because high house prices had kept them in small spaces.

rows.title: The Fed’s favorite inflation measure showed price hikes are at their slowest rate since late 2020
rows.standfirst: Prices rose at a 3% annual rate in October with core prices growing 3.5%, according to the personal consumption expenditures price index.

rows.title: Wall Street titans are getting behind Nikki Haley in the presidential race—billionaire hedge funder Bill Ackman says it’s time for Biden to ‘step aside’
rows.standfirst: Many in the finance industry “are looking to consolidate around an alternative to Trump before it’s too late,” said one expert.

rows.title: Williams Sonoma’s CEO defied the retail apocalypse. Now a gloomy economy is forcing even her well-off customers to spend less
rows.standfirst: CEO Laura Alber is exploring new revenue streams as inflation and a housing slowdown test the West Elm and Pottery Barn parent.

rows.title: The Fed’s favorite inflation gauge cooled in October, and Wall Street believes it may signal ‘interest rate cuts are on the horizon’
rows.standfirst: The Fed’s favorite inflation gauge cooled in October, giving investors hope that the central bank’s more than 20-month-long interest rate hiking campaign is coming to an end.

rows.title: ‘Why am I paying 6%?’ As New York’s real-estate market slows, industry faces showdown over who pays agents’ fees
rows.standfirst: After a bombshell jury decision that found the structure of broker fees illegal, New York faces its own lawsuits.

rows.title: Housing affordability is the worst it’s been in decades. It will improve in 2024, but by only a ‘small step,’ Realtor.com chief economist says
rows.standfirst: Mortgage rates are expected to drop modestly to 6.8% in 2024.
